title: Fecundity analysis
text: Fecundity chondrichthyans — number utero embryos carried gravid female — typically increases maternal body size. fecundity() fits simplest description relationship, ordinary linear regression: Fi=+b⋅Li+ϵ,ϵ∼N(0,σ2)F_i = + b \cdot L_i + \epsilon, \quad \epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2) FiF_i number embryos carried female ii LiL_i length (age). slope bb increase litter size per unit length, usually quantity interest.

title: Fecundity analysis
text: fecundity count zero means animal gravid, fecundity zero. Including records bias intercept downwards inflate slope. fecundity() therefore drops records zero negative counts fitting reports many removed. Predictions span length age range gravid animals .

title: Fecundity analysis
text: summary reports intercept aa slope bb standard errors, coefficient determination, p-value slope, residual standard deviation σ\sigma, sample size, mean range observed fecundity, predictor range model applies.
code: library(mustelus) #> Welcome to mustelus package data(spottail)  fec <- fecundity(emb, length, data = spottail) summary(fec) #> # A tibble: 1 × 11 #>       a a.Std.Error       b b.Std.Error r.squared  p.value Sigma     n mean.fec #>   <dbl> <chr>         <dbl> <chr>           <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <int>    <dbl> #> 1 -7.75 ( 1.24 )    0.00946 ( 0.00108 )     0.527 7.97e-13 0.682    71     3.06 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: fec.range <chr>, x.range <chr>

title: Fecundity analysis
text: plot() returns named list ggplot objects, one per group. solid line fitted mean, dashed ribbon 95% confidence interval, dotted ribbon 95% prediction interval — presentation used Walker (2005).  len_weight(), two interval types answer different questions. confidence interval describes uncertainty mean litter size given length narrows data accumulate; prediction interval describes spread litter sizes expect observe individual females, narrow appreciably. predicting reproductive output female known size, prediction interval relevant one.
code: p <- plot(fec) p$Unspecified + xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Number of embryos")

title: Length-weight analysis
text: relationship body mass length fishes typically described power curve: Wi=αLiβW_i = \alpha L_i^{\beta} WiW_i LiL_i weight length individual ii, α\alpha β\beta estimated parameters. Individual variability weight also increases length, multiplicative rather additive error structure appropriate: Wi=αLiβeϵ,ϵ∼N(0,σ2)W_i = \alpha L_i^{\beta} e^{\epsilon}, \quad \epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2) Upon log-transformation becomes standard linear regression: ln⁡(Wi)=ln⁡(α)+β⋅ln⁡(Li)+ϵ\ln(W_i) = \ln(\alpha) + \beta \cdot \ln(L_i) + \epsilon ln⁡(α)\ln(\alpha) intercept β\beta slope. model fitted len_weight().

title: Length-weight analysis
text: subtle important consequence log-transforming response back-transforming predictions gives median weight given length, mean. lognormal distribution, mean : E[W∣L]=eμ̂+σ2/2E[W \mid L] = e^{\hat{\mu} + \sigma^2/2} σ2\sigma^2 residual variance. len_weight() applies correction automatically — predicted values intervals corrected back-transformation bias.

title: Length-weight analysis
text: summary table reports: intercept natural scale (=eln⁡(α)= e^{\ln(\alpha)}), standard error range, slope bb, standard error, residual standard deviation σ\sigma, log-likelihood, sample size, length range.
code: library(mustelus) #> Welcome to mustelus package data(spottail)  lw <- len_weight(wgt, length, data = spottail) summary(lw) #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>          a Std.Error.range      b Std.Error Sigma    LL     n len.range  #>      <dbl> <chr>            <dbl> <chr>     <dbl> <dbl> <int> <chr>      #> 1 2.13e-10 ( 1.441 - 3.16 )  3.47 ( 0.057 ) 0.102  166.   192 478 - 1301

title: Length-weight analysis
text: plot() returns named list ggplot objects — one per group — can customised standard ggplot2 calls. solid line predicted mean, dashed ribbon 95% confidence interval, dotted ribbon 95% prediction interval.
code: p <- plot(lw_sex) p$f + xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Weight (kg)") p$m + xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Weight (kg)")

title: Length-weight analysis
text: interval types appear output. answer different questions: Confidence interval — uncertainty mean weight given length. Narrows data. Prediction interval — expected spread individual weights given length. Reflects biological variability captured σ\sigma narrow appreciably data. fisheries reporting purposes prediction interval informative, describes range weights expect observe field.

title: Length-weight analysis
text: function accepts positive numeric predictor — fork length, precaudal length, measurement makes biological sense log-transform.
code: lw_fl <- len_weight(wgt, FL, data = spottail) summary(lw_fl) #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>               a Std.Error.range       b Std.Error  Sigma    LL     n len.range  #>           <dbl> <chr>             <dbl> <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <int> <chr>      #> 1 0.00000000249 ( 1.782 - 3.485 )  3.22 ( 0.05 )  0.0940  172.   181 358 - 1015

title: Length-weight analysis
text: result nested tibble one row per group. List columns data, coefs, preds, mods named group level direct access: preds data frame contains six columns: length, weight (bias-corrected mean), clower/cupper (95% confidence interval), plower/pupper (95% prediction interval).

title: Length at maturity analysis
text: Three styles raw data display available:
code: # Proportions (default) — point size scaled by n per bin plot(lm50, raw_data = "proportions")$Unspecified +   xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Proportion mature") # Point — same bins, uniform point size plot(lm50, raw_data = "point")$Unspecified +   xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Proportion mature") # Rug — mature individuals on top, immature on bottom plot(lm50, raw_data = "rug")$Unspecified +   xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Proportion mature")

title: Length at maturity analysis
text: binwidth argument controls width bins data units (default range/10):
code: plot(lm50, binwidth = 50)$Unspecified +   xlab("Total length (mm)") + ylab("Proportion mature")
